It imports the key ARN, the VPC id, the flow-logs role ARN and the runtime role ARN, and exports the six contract outputs.

findings.finding: AWS::CloudTrail::Trail: IsLogging and S3BucketName required; the key property is spelled KMSKeyId; TrailName change requires replacement; EnableLogFileValidation and IsMultiRegionTrail default false; takes Tags; the page is inconsistent on what Ref returns, so the TrailArn output uses Fn::GetAtt Arn; no DependsOn note (the template sets DependsOn on the bucket policy, as CloudTrail must be able to write when the trail is created). AWS::EC2::FlowLog: ResourceId and ResourceType (VPC allowed) required; MaxAggregationInterval 60 or 600, default 600; DeliverLogsPermissionArn required for cloud-watch-logs; every property but Tags requires replacement; takes Tags; Ref returns the flow-log id. AWS::Logs::LogGroup: KmsKeyId is a key or alias ARN; RetentionInDays 90 allowed; LogGroupName change requires replacement; takes Tags; Fn::GetAtt Arn ends with ':*'. AWS::S3::Bucket: takes Tags; BucketName change requires replacement; only empty buckets delete; KMSMasterKeyID should be a full key ARN. AWS::S3::BucketPolicy is already in UNTAGGABLE_TYPES, so the template guard is unchanged.
findings.basis: CloudFormation template reference pages for the five types and for S3 Rule and ServerSideEncryptionRule, read 2026-10-26; tools/aws_template_guard.py.

findings.finding: S3: a PutObject that sends x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms without x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id is encrypted with the AWS managed key; the condition key s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id takes a key ARN of the form arn:aws:kms:region:acct-id:key/key-id; a PUT without encryption headers gets the bucket's default encryption.
findings.basis: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html and the ServerSideEncryptionRule reference page, read 2026-10-26.

findings.finding: S3 Object Ownership: new buckets are BucketOwnerEnforced by default; with ACLs disabled the bucket still accepts PUTs that specify the bucket-owner-full-control canned ACL. CloudTrail's recommended single-account bucket policy is the v1 AclCheck and Write statements (aws:SourceArn; s3:x-amz-acl bucket-owner-full-control; resource <bucket>/<prefix>/AWSLogs/<account>/*); the CloudTrail page does not mention Object Ownership or SSE-KMS deny statements.

The v1 trail delivered log files and digest files under the same DenyUnencryptedObjects statement (LatestDeliveryTime and LatestDigestDeliveryTime set), so CloudTrail sends the aws:kms encryption header with a trail key; v1 granted CloudTrail no kms:Decrypt.

The IAM SimulatePrincipalPolicy reference states 'Simulation of resource-based policies isn't supported for IAM roles'. A simulation of the runtime role against the deploy bucket policy is therefore not used as R7 evidence; the bucket-side limits on the runtime role are evidenced by the policy read back (step 08) and exercised by live calls from the host (R11, R12b).

Round 2 (2026-10-26, ~17:44-17:47 UTC): the stack proposal-orchestrator-audit was created without rollback; the trail was created and started logging with a key policy that grants CloudTrail no kms:Decrypt and a trail bucket without an S3 Bucket Key (R6-D10 holds at creation); S3 accepted the deploy bucket policy with NotResource; both bucket policies read back equal the resolved template; the flow log on the VPC is ACTIVE with DeliverLogsStatus SUCCESS; a header-less PUT to bundles/ was encrypted with the CMK and the Bucket Key, while PUTs with AES256 and with aws:kms but no key id were refused by an explicit deny in the bucket policy (S3 does not fill the encryption condition keys from the bucket default); S3 reports BlockedEncryptionTypes SSE-C on both buckets as its own default.

decisions.question: Trail bucket encryption (handoff section 4, point 1)
decisions.answer: Default encryption SSE-KMS with the imported KeyArn and BucketKeyEnabled false (R6-D10); the trail's own KMSKeyId is the same KeyArn.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '1a'. 'The bucket shows the CMK' then holds for the bucket configuration and for every object.
decisions.consequence: Without a Bucket Key every trail object costs KMS requests (paid from credits; R14 counts them).

decisions.question: Deny unencrypted objects (point 2)
decisions.answer: 2a: the trail bucket keeps the v1 DenyUnencryptedObjects statement (deny s3:PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms). 2b (b): the deploy bucket refuses a PUT whose encryption header is not aws:kms, a PUT that names aws:kms without a key id, and a PUT that names another key id than KeyArn; a PUT without encryption headers is not refused and gets the bucket default (the CMK).
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '2 = 2a igen + 2b (b)'. F-R7-4: without a key id S3 would use the AWS managed key, so the v1 form on the deploy bucket would push uploads to the wrong key.
decisions.consequence: R15 uploads to bundles/ without encryption headers (or with --sse aws:kms and --sse-kms-key-id KeyArn).

decisions.question: Deploy bucket policy (point 3)
decisions.answer: (b): deny-only. DenyInsecureTransport; DenyPrincipalsOutsideAccount (aws:PrincipalAccount); the three encryption denies of R7-D2; for the runtime role (ArnEquals aws:PrincipalArn = the imported RuntimeRoleArn) DenyRuntimeRoleExceptBundlesRead (NotAction GetObject, ListBucket, GetBucketLocation), DenyRuntimeRoleGetOutsideBundles (NotResource bundles/*) and DenyRuntimeRoleListOutsideBundles (StringNotLike s3:prefix bundles/*). No Allow statement. BucketKeyEnabled true.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '3 (b)'. In the same account a bucket-policy Allow would duplicate R5's identity policy; the denies make 'access limited to the runtime role's prefixes' true on the bucket side, independently of IAM.
decisions.consequence: The admin role keeps full in-account access through IAM; any AWS service that would need the bucket would be refused by DenyPrincipalsOutsideAccount and needs a successor record.

decisions.question: Retention (point 4)
decisions.answer: DeletionPolicy and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain on both buckets and the flow-log group; the trail, the flow log and the two bucket policies go with the stack.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '4a'. Audit data must outlive the stack; a non-empty bucket blocks deletion anyway.
decisions.consequence: The audit stack is not deleted: recreating it would collide with the retained names. Retiring a bucket or the group is a manual step with a successor record.

decisions.question: Flow-log scope (point 5)
decisions.answer: (a): one flow log on the VPC (ResourceType VPC, the imported VpcId), TrafficType ALL, LogDestinationType cloud-watch-logs to the group, DeliverLogsPermissionArn the imported FlowLogsRoleArn, default record format, MaxAggregationInterval 600.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '5 (a) 600 s'. One flow log covers every subnet, present and future, and matches the contract's single FlowLogId.
decisions.consequence: DC-08 ('on every subnet') is evidenced by describe-flow-logs on the VPC together with the VPC's subnet list.

decisions.question: Trail settings (point 6)
decisions.answer: Trail ${ProjectName}-bedrock-trail, single-Region with home eu-north-1, IncludeGlobalServiceEvents true, EnableLogFileValidation true, IsLogging true, S3KeyPrefix cloudtrail/${ProjectName}, KMSKeyId the imported KeyArn, no EventSelectors or AdvancedEventSelectors (default: management events, read and write, no data events), DependsOn the trail bucket policy.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '6a'; R6-D2 fixes name, ARN and home Region; v1 had no custom selectors.
decisions.consequence: Whether eu. profile Converse calls appear as management events is DC-26, shown by R11.

decisions.question: Trail-bucket lifecycle (point 7)
decisions.answer: One rule on prefix cloudtrail/${ProjectName}/: transition after 90 days to GLACIER_IR, expiration after 365 days, noncurrent versions expire 30 days after becoming noncurrent.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '7a'; the v1 rule with new names.
decisions.consequence: In the versioned bucket, expiration adds a delete marker; the object version is removed 30 days later, about 395 days after delivery.

The template guard is unchanged (F-R7-3).

The audit test asserts that the stack's imports equal the exports whose consumers name R7.

decisions.question: Object Ownership (point 12)
decisions.answer: Both buckets set OwnershipControls ObjectOwnership BucketOwnerEnforced explicitly.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '12a'; F-R7-5: the default for new buckets, and PUTs with bucket-owner-full-control (CloudTrail's) are still accepted.
decisions.consequence: get-bucket-ownership-controls is part of the evidence.

decisions.question: Deploy-bucket lifecycle (point 13)
decisions.answer: One rule on the whole bucket: noncurrent versions expire after 30 days; incomplete multipart uploads abort after 7 days; current versions do not expire.
decisions.consequence: A replaced bundle stays recoverable for 30 days.

decisions.question: DC-30 scope (point 14)
decisions.answer: DC-30 covers every log group in eu-north-1; before R7 there is none (F-R7-1), after R7 exactly the flow-log group.
decisions.consequence: A log group created later by a service (for example a CloudFormation or SSM default group) falls under DC-30 and needs the CMK and at most 90-day retention, or a register note.

decisions.question: DC-24 evidence (point 15)
decisions.answer: Besides LogFileValidationEnabled and LatestDigestDeliveryTime, one aws cloudtrail validate-logs run by the admin role over the delivered files in the delivery round.
decisions.consequence: Needs at least one digest file (hourly), so it belongs to round 3.

decisions.question: Key id pinned on the trail bucket (point 16)
decisions.answer: No: the trail bucket keeps the v1 statement only; it does not require a specific kms key id.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '16a'. The format in which CloudTrail sends the key id header is not documented on the pages read; a wrong pin would stop delivery silently.
decisions.consequence: The trail's KMSKeyId and the trail bucket's default encryption name the CMK; evidence shows both.

decisions.question: Test the deploy bucket's encryption denies before R15 (point 17, added by the agent)
decisions.answer: Yes. In round 2 the admin role puts three small objects with a fixed test text under bundles/: without encryption headers (expected: accepted, SSE-KMS with KeyArn and the Bucket Key), with --server-side-encryption AES256 and with --server-side-encryption aws:kms without a key id (both expected: AccessDenied). The accepted object's version is then deleted by version id, leaving no object and no delete marker.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '17 a'. Closes the R7-D2 known gap (whether S3 fills the encryption condition keys from the bucket default for a header-less PUT) before R15 depends on it.
decisions.consequence: A refused header-less upload or an accepted AES256 / key-less upload is a FAIL: successor record and an UPDATE change set of the deploy bucket policy.

decisions.question: DC-08 before the VPC has any network interface (point 18, added by the agent)
decisions.answer: (a): DC-08 is VERIFIED_PASS on configuration: one flow log on the VPC (covering its one subnet), TrafficType ALL, to the CMK-encrypted /proposal-orchestrator/vpc-flow-logs group, FlowLogStatus ACTIVE and DeliverLogsStatus SUCCESS. The register note states that delivered flow-log records are shown by R11.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '18a'. Before R11 the VPC has no network interface, so no flow-log record or log stream can exist; waiting would hold R7 open on a condition only R11 creates.
decisions.consequence: R11 evidences a flow-log stream and records; the R5-D4 known gap (scoped logs:DescribeLogGroups) closes there, and a FAILED delivery there leads to a successor record and an UPDATE of the iam stack.

known_gaps.gap: That the trail is created and delivers without a CloudTrail kms:Decrypt grant when the bucket has no S3 Bucket Key (R6-D10 known gap; F-R7-6 supports it). A refusal at creation stops R7: successor record, UPDATE of the kms stack first.

Whether S3 fills the encryption condition keys from the bucket's default encryption for a PUT that sends no encryption header. If it fills s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption but not the key id, DenyKmsHeaderWithoutKeyId would refuse header-less uploads. Shown by the round-2 test uploads (R7-D17); a refusal leads to a successor record and an UPDATE. Closed in round 2 (F-R7-8).

That S3 accepts NotResource in a bucket policy statement whose NotResource lies inside the bucket. A refusal at PutBucketPolicy fails the stack creation; the two retained buckets may then remain and need a follow-up step sheet. Closed in round 2: the policy was accepted (F-R7-8).
That the runtime-role denies of the deploy bucket policy refuse writes and reads outside bundles/ in practice (F-R7-7: not simulated). Shown by live calls from the host in R11/R12b.

Whether logs:DescribeLogGroups scoped to the one group's ARN suffices for flow-log delivery (R5-D4 known gap). Shown by DeliverLogsStatus and a log stream. Not shown in R7: no network interface exists before R11 (R7-D18); R11 shows it.

The AWS-managed organization's RCPs, which can apply to S3 and KMS, are not visible from the member account (OD11-r2 known gap). A restriction shows as an explicit deny at the change set or at creation.

not_evidence_of: That the deploy bucket's runtime-role denies hold for live calls from the host (R11, R12b; F-R7-7).
That flow-log records are delivered (R11; R7-D18).
That Bedrock Converse calls appear in the trail (DC-26, R11).
